alg: Build a 2x2x2 block, then extend to 2x2x3. After the 2x2x2 block there are 3 sides to extend on, explore all of them.
When inserting F2L pairs do not stay stuck with speedcubing muscle memory, try several alternative insertions and compare their move counts.
Example: scramble R F' D2 U inverted is U' D2 F R'. Find a good solution on the inverted scramble, then invert the solution, it solves the original scramble.

Perform a move that belongs at the end of the solution before the scramble, e.g. pseudo F2L needing a final D becomes D in front: D D' L' U' L D. Newest premove goes first, the premove must still be undone at the end of the real solution.

Normal Inverse Scramble Switch, Guus Razoux Schultz 2009. Solve on the normal scramble until stuck, switch to the inverse scramble, and back. Rule: if piece X was where piece Y belongs before switching, Y will be where X belongs after switching.

Reverse NISS uses the moves of the skeleton after the chosen point plus the scramble as premoves, then applies the solution up to that point, to recognize the remaining case, e.g. a PLL. Usually combined with insertions.
Walk the solution and find spots where no 2x2x2 pieces sit on U, insert U, U' or U2 there and check whether a better continuation appears.

Solve everything except 3 to 5 corners, then insert 8 move corner commutators earlier in the solution where they cancel moves. Edge cycles are used less since slices cost 2 moves in HTM. Track pieces with stickers.
Short flexible insertion algs: R' L F2 R L' U2 plus variants R' F2 R L' U2 L, L F2 L' R U2 R', F2 R L' U2 R' L. Commutators: minimum 8 HTM corners, 10 HTM edges.

Insertion move counts from Tronto FMC tutorial v3 page 33: corner 3-cycle 5/6, edge 3-cycle 7, 2 twisted corners 8, 3 twisted corners 9, 4 corners double swap 9/10, 4 corners 3 plus 1 twisted 10, corner 5-cycle 10/11, 2 corners 2 edges double 2-cycle 10.

Skeleton names: C corners, E edges, T twisted corners, F flipped edges, X centers, number prefix for cycles or swaps, e.g. 3c, 3t, 2c2e, 5e, 2e2e, 4x, 3e2f. 2c2c and 3c1t are both commonly called 4c. Old names prefixed AB for All But.
Reduce to the domino group, 180 degree only turns, a step of Thistlethwaite's algorithm. Widely adopted by top solvers since 2019.
Solve blocks freely without a pattern, leave at most 4 edges and 4 corners, conjugate them onto one face, then finish with premoves or a second cube.
Learn short last layer algs up to about 10 moves knowing exactly what they do to corners and edges: the one 6-move alg, three 7-move, five 8-move, and so on.

Standard moves only, no rotations slices or wide moves. Fixed up and front colors. Write down promising moves early. Make a backup solve. Practice fast scrambling. Bring stickers and a second cube for insertions.

Pseudo blocks have colors that do not match surrounding pieces. Non-matching blocks misalign centers only. Passive blockbuilding allows wrong orientation inside blocks. Domino blockbuilding restricts to 180 degree turns.
